authoringContext.note: This checklist defines the activation workflow. It does not claim that the authoring base or a future release candidate is production-ready.

commandCatalog.instruction: If the final release SHA contains a named RC validation package script, record and run that exact script. Do not invent a command.
Select and record the current supported authenticated Supabase ledger-export procedure. The authoring base does not pin or install a hosted CLI.
Use the exact dry-run mode of the operator-approved Supabase migration runner and record tool, version, target identity, invocation, and plan without credentials.
Use the same operator-approved Supabase migration runner whose dry-run exactly matched approvedMigrationEntries. The authoring base supplies no copy-paste hosted apply command.

migrationApprovalModel.approvedEntriesRule: The concrete ordered entries copied into operatorRecord.approvedMigrationEntries after Phase 1 reconciliation are the only entries approved for Phase 2.
migrationApprovalModel.historicalBaselineRule: Historical-equivalent objects are never replayed. Any ledger baseline operation requires separate explicit approval and the current supported Supabase history procedure.
migrationApprovalModel.newExecutableRule: Only manifest entries whose exact version, filename, canonical checksum, dependency, marker transition, and hosted absence all match may be applied.
migrationApprovalModel.mismatchRule: Any mismatch, extra hosted migration, ambiguous history, missing dependency, or changed checksum stops the line.
migrationApprovalModel.applyMechanism: An operator-approved, version-recorded Supabase migration runner applies the tracked migration directory to the independently verified project after its exact dry-run matches approvedMigrationEntries. The authoring base does not pin or install a hosted CLI, so the exact supported tool and invocation must be selected during authorization. No SQL copy/paste and no ad hoc ledger mutation are permitted.

phases.entryCondition: A named final RC branch and immutable release SHA exist locally.
phases.exitCondition: Unified local production preflight returns READY_FOR_HOSTED_PREFLIGHT and every other local gate is green.

steps.action: Open a bounded activation record and capture the release SHA, release branch, operator refs, change record, and planned authorization boundaries.
Verify the RC worktree is clean, HEAD equals the recorded release SHA, and no generated or untracked source is required for the build.
Reconcile the final integration inventory against the RC and prove every approved source commit is an ancestor or otherwise recorded in the final reviewed diff.
Run the migration reconciliation planner and Admin R3 migration identity checks; require unique numeric versions, exact manifest/file mapping, dependency order, markers, and canonical checksums.
Run the complete root test gate without exclusions or assertion weakening.
Run the repository TypeScript gate.
Build the production artifact and scan the built client for direct provider routes, server-only environment names, credential-shaped literals, preview adapters, and synthetic production authority.
Run secondary package gates including Student Runtime, prototype UI, and final assembly browser projects; retain desktop/mobile, accessibility, keyboard, reduced-motion, and recovery results.
evidence: manual accessibility/device record if required by the RC

steps.action: Require the Study production security/adversarial R4 files on the release SHA and run their exact Netlify and database suites.
Require the Study recovery/chaos gate on the release SHA and run its uncertain-commit, replay, refresh, stale-revision, content-loss, and immutable-binding scenarios.
Require and run the local Study production smoke harness from the release SHA; require zero external-contact attempts and STUDY_LOCAL_PRODUCTION_SMOKE_READY.
Run Admin Production Preflight R3, Study deployment-environment preflight, migration reconciliation, and the unified local production preflight in a value-silent environment.
Discover whether the release SHA contains a named final RC validation harness. If present, run its exact repository command; if absent, record that fact and do not invent one.
Confirm the unified result is exactly READY_FOR_HOSTED_PREFLIGHT and freeze all Phase 0 artifacts to the release SHA.

phases.entryCondition: Phase 0 is green and authorization names the exact Supabase project and Netlify site.
phases.exitCondition: Hosted state exactly matches the release expectations; no write occurred.

steps.action: Record a read-only authorization naming the exact project, site, operator, time window, and permitted queries. Verify no migration, configuration, deploy, secret read, or provider call is authorized.
Verify Supabase organization, project reference, environment, database host, and API hostname from authenticated hosted state against the approved Manuel Academy target.
Export the hosted migration ledger read-only and reconcile every version with the release-SHA manifest. Classify equivalent historical objects separately from executable missing migrations.

Read-only compare markers, relation kinds, columns, constraints, indexes, functions, owners, search paths, policies, triggers, grants, forced-RLS state, required roles/extensions, exposed schemas, and candidate-name collisions.

Record count-only owner/admin assignment state and bootstrap readiness. Do not record user IDs or email addresses. If no reviewed owner bootstrap or owner-management path exists for the observed state, stop.
Verify required Netlify environment variable names, scopes, and context presence only; verify public URL/anon configuration points to the same project without copying values.

Verify Netlify team/site identity, production branch, deploy contexts, auto-publish behavior, build/publish/functions configuration, Node version, redirects, schedule, current production deploy ID, and commit ref. Resolve the repository main/master documentation conflict from hosted truth.
evidence: current deploy ID and commit ref

steps.action: Compare all hosted evidence with expected state. Any difference, unknown, partial ledger, or missing prerequisite ends the phase as STOPPED without a write.

phases.entryCondition: Phase 1 matched exactly, a backup is restorable, and the concrete ordered migration list is approved.
phases.exitCondition: Every approved entry committed in order and all post-apply checks pass.

steps.action: Copy the concrete release-manifest entries into approvedMigrationEntries with version, filename, checksum, dependency, marker transition, hosted pre-state, and approved action. Approve exactly that ordered list.
Verify a fresh restorable database backup or platform recovery point, recovery owner, retention window, restore target, and rehearsed recovery procedure before any mutation.
Resolve historical-equivalent objects through a separately approved current supported Supabase history procedure without replaying their SQL. Re-read the ledger and objects afterward.
Run the linked-project migration dry-run and require its exact order to equal approvedMigrationEntries with no extra, skipped, repeated, or changed entry.
Confirm new Study entry, new provider calls, and worker claims are dark or fail-closed for the migration window while audit and incident evidence remain available.
Apply only the approved tracked migrations through the linked-project Supabase CLI. One unexpected prompt, plan difference, checksum difference, or transaction failure stops further application.

Re-read ledger, markers, object definitions, owners, search paths, RLS/FORCE, grants, policies, triggers, constraints, indexes, object counts, private-schema exposure, and exact denial probes. Verify no partial object or unexpected grant exists.

On any failure, stop consumers and workers, preserve evidence, classify transaction rollback versus post-commit fault, and open a forward-repair review. Do not continue to later migrations unless the line is re-authorized.

phases.entryCondition: Phase 2 is verified and configuration owners have approved value sources without exposing values to the activation record.
phases.exitCondition: All required names are present in correct scopes, durable configuration is revisioned, and fail-closed gates are verified.

steps.action: Approve a name/scope/source/revision plan for every environment and durable configuration input. Evidence contains names, presence, scope, revision, and verification reference only.

Publish independently verified effective-dated provider pricing terms through the owner-authorized preview/commit path. Match provider, product, model, logical tier, usage unit, currency, unit size, IntegerMicros rate, interval, revision, and verification reference. Missing or ambiguous billable pricing remains unavailable, never zero.

Set AI/TTS deployment ceilings, server-only provider credential presence, model/tier policy, logical voice catalog and private voice allowlist. Enable premium TTS only when an approved catalog mapping exists; otherwise retain browser fallback and disabled synthesis.

Configure the Study client/server gates, matching Supabase public/server identities, safety limiter secret presence, provider secret presence, proxy-only mode, and preview/browser-provider-key prohibitions exactly as the Study deployment preflight requires.

Configure worker identity, credential ID/version, configuration version, credential presence, manual invocation secret presence, exact five-minute scheduled function, least-privilege registry scopes, and production composition readiness. Keep external email/SMS routes unavailable unless separately governed and approved.

Bind ACADEMY_APP_VERSION to the immutable release identifier and record independently versioned Tutor, Jarvis, and TTS engine values where applicable. Require host COMMIT_REF to equal releaseSha after deployment.

Record intended client/server Study, AI, TTS, worker, curriculum pointer, and cohort states. Durable provider enablement must remain bounded by deployment ceilings and all safety/authorization/readiness gates.
Re-run value-silent configuration/preflight checks and freeze the configuration state record for deployment.

phases.entryCondition: Migration and configuration records are frozen, and hosted Netlify trigger behavior is verified.
phases.exitCondition: One production deploy is published with deploy commit ref equal to releaseSha and immediate readiness checks pass.

steps.action: Approve the release SHA, verified migration state, verified configuration state, Netlify site ID, production branch, deploy context, and rollback deploy ID as one deployment packet.

Use only the hosted-verified Netlify production trigger: the verified auto-publish branch or the verified manual production deploy control. Do not infer the branch from conflicting repository documentation.
Trigger one controlled production deploy for the approved release SHA. Do not clear caches or trigger a second build unless a new authorization records why.
Verify site/team/context, deploy ID, deploy commit ref, release SHA, build command, publish/functions paths, Node version, redirects, function inventory, schedule, and configuration-state linkage.

Before broad navigation, verify the application shell, service-worker version, Admin authorization boundary, Study readiness boundary, and worker health return bounded expected states without secret or private-data exposure.

phases.entryCondition: Deploy identity is exact and operator-safe synthetic identities/data are available.
phases.exitCondition: Every smoke family passes with no stop condition and the release is accepted or rolled back.

steps.action: Use an approved operator/admin account and synthetic/operator-safe learner fixture. Never require or copy real learner content into smoke evidence.
Open /academy/admin and verify Admin shell authorization, navigation, Overview data freshness/completeness labels, and denial for an unassigned or insufficient-role account.

Verify Audit pagination/filtering and Configuration effective revisions, deployment ceilings, protective disable behavior, and no credential/raw-row exposure. Do not perform an unplanned configuration mutation.

Verify Engine Performance, System Health, Costs, and Provider Pricing show honest completeness, exact versions, exact decimal-string money, correct thresholds, configured pricing intervals, and unavailable rather than invented zero when evidence is absent.

Verify Study Operations worker/backlog/readiness evidence and Curriculum Studio published/draft/validation/release state within the operator's capabilities. Confirm immutable published artifacts and current active pointer.

Open /study-engine for the synthetic learner, verify server-derived authority, ready/unavailable honesty, route refresh behavior, learner-switch cancellation, logout cancellation, and no preview or synthetic-authority fallback.

Begin one synthetic Study session, verify exact published release/settings binding and bound content, checkpoint safely, refresh/resume, and test an idempotent replay. Do not complete or rewrite an existing real learner session.

Verify the private scheduled function cadence and one bounded worker run evidence record. Confirm credential/config versions, one claim/attempt path, duplicate suppression, and no unverified delivered claim. Use manual invocation only when separately authorized.
Verify one synthetic operational event and provider-attempt/cost path is delivered and aggregated exactly once with correct app/engine/curriculum versions and privacy-safe dimensions.

Run authorized/unauthorized/cross-household/forged-role probes against Admin and Study boundaries. Inspect browser network and bundles for secret values, provider credentials, private notes, learner answers, Tutor content, raw provider bodies, and backend errors.

Verify /academy/admin and /study-engine deep links/refreshes, SPA fallback, 320px/390px reflow, touch targets, keyboard focus, reduced motion, and service-worker update on an approved desktop and mobile-class browser.
Review all stop conditions. Record PRODUCTION_SMOKE_ACCEPTED only when every smoke step passes; otherwise execute the bounded rollback matrix and record STOPPED.

phases.entryCondition: A stop condition, smoke failure, or operator rollback decision occurs.
phases.exitCondition: New risk is contained, evidence is preserved, and the resulting deploy/configuration/migration state is recorded.

steps.action: Stop new Study entry, new provider work, and new worker claims as applicable before changing artifacts. Preserve attempts, receipts, proposals, telemetry, and audit evidence.
Select the smallest compatible rollback control from rollbackMatrix and record its preconditions, owner, expected scope, and verification plan.

Treat committed database migrations as forward-only unless an independently reviewed recovery plan proves otherwise. Use an additive forward repair for post-commit defects; never rewrite existing Study bindings or erase evidence.

phases.exitCondition: The bounded evidence packet is complete and contains no secrets or learner content.

steps.action: Capture release SHA, deploy ID/commit ref, migration versions/hashes, preflight result, configuration revisions/presence, smoke result, bounded error/reason codes, final state, and timestamps.
Review the packet and remove any secret value, token, credential, learner content, Tutor conversation, provider body, contact value, or raw database error before distribution.
Record the final decision, current deploy/configuration/migration state, remaining follow-up owners, and whether activation is accepted or held.

rollbackMatrix.trigger: Application regression with schema compatibility preserved
rollbackMatrix.control: Publish the previously recorded green immutable Netlify deploy through the verified production control.
verification: deploy ID changed to approved rollback ID

rollbackMatrix.control: Disable the server Study gate immediately and the client Study gate in the next controlled build; keep preview and browser-provider-key modes off.

rollbackMatrix.trigger: Duplicate, unauthorized, indeterminate, or unsafe worker behavior
rollbackMatrix.control: Stop new scheduled/manual claims using the verified Netlify schedule control and worker readiness/credential controls; do not erase leases, attempts, receipts, or jobs.

rollbackMatrix.trigger: Provider safety, pricing, accounting, credential, or output risk
rollbackMatrix.control: Set deployment and durable AI/TTS enablement to false through approved controls. Rotate a credential only when compromise requires it; never record the value.
verification: no quota or ledger mutation on denied calls

rollbackMatrix.control: Use the owner-authorized audited release operation to point new resolution to a previously published immutable release.

rollbackMatrix.trigger: Unexpected behavior in sessions created against the newly active release
rollbackMatrix.control: Disable new Study begins while changing the active pointer to the prior published release, then re-enable only after smoke. Already-bound Study sessions remain pinned to their original immutable release and settings snapshot.
verification: resume resolves each session's stored release

rollbackMatrix.trigger: Post-commit migration defect or incompatible live behavior
rollbackMatrix.control: Keep consumers dark, preserve evidence, and ship a separately reviewed additive forward repair. A failed transaction is verified as rolled back; a committed migration is not treated as trivially reversible.
verification: post-repair catalog and denial probes pass

stopTheLine.trigger: Any release file, manifest, dry-run, hosted ledger, or recorded checksum differs
stopTheLine.action: Stop before further migration or deploy work and require a new reviewed migration plan.

stopTheLine.trigger: Hosted ledger contains an extra, partial, reordered, or unknown version
stopTheLine.action: Stop read-only; do not hide, overwrite, replay, or bypass the history.

stopTheLine.trigger: Admin, guardian, learner, worker, or service operation permits too much, denies the required operator unexpectedly, or uses caller-authored authority
stopTheLine.action: Disable the affected entry point and preserve bounded denial evidence.

stopTheLine.trigger: Any secret, credential, contact, learner content, Tutor conversation, provider body, raw SQL/error, or private note crosses an unauthorized boundary
stopTheLine.action: Contain the surface, revoke/rotate only if required, preserve minimized evidence, and begin privacy incident handling.

stopTheLine.trigger: A provider/product/model/tier/unit/currency/rate/interval or account-specific term is missing, ambiguous, stale, or incorrect
stopTheLine.action: Disable the affected provider path; never substitute a default or zero cost.

stopTheLine.trigger: IntegerMicros calculation, rounding, threshold, component, request-unit, or aggregate result differs from the approved fixture
stopTheLine.action: Disable affected provider work and cost reporting until corrected and reconciled.

stopTheLine.trigger: Preview/synthetic/caller-authored identity, role, release, settings, revision, or content becomes production authority
stopTheLine.action: Disable Study immediately and preserve bounded authority reason codes.

stopTheLine.trigger: More than one provider effect or delivered claim occurs for one attempt/idempotency identity
stopTheLine.action: Stop worker claims and provider delivery, retain all immutable evidence, and reconcile before re-enable.

stopTheLine.trigger: One logical event/attempt is persisted or aggregated more than once, or replay changes its facts
stopTheLine.action: Stop affected reporting/provider activation and reconcile writer, ledger, and aggregate identities.

stopTheLine.trigger: Any required Phase 5 check fails, is unavailable unexpectedly, leaks data, or cannot prove the expected state
stopTheLine.action: Do not accept the release; select the smallest rollback control.

stopTheLine.trigger: A resumed session re-resolves a pointer/settings snapshot, or an active-pointer rollback rewrites an existing session
stopTheLine.action: Disable new Study entry, preserve the affected opaque references, and roll back application/pointer for new sessions only.
